1.title: Self Driving Products: Product Signals to Pull Requests — Joshua Snyder, PostHog
1.author: AI Engineer
1.hook: PostHog is building an agent pipeline that converts product signals (errors, session replays, analytics anomalies) directly into reviewed/shipped PRs, skipping the human dashboard-reading step entirely — with concrete implementation details on signal ingestion, grouping, research agents, and safety filtering.

1.title: Sovereign Escape Velocity: Ownership w Open Models — Gus Martins, & Ian Ballantyne, Google DeepMind
1.author: AI Engineer
1.hook: Gemma 2 (26B/31B) achieves 4th/7th ranked open-model performance while being 2–20× smaller than competitors, with the 31B running on a single GPU vs. competitors needing 4–5 GPUs—concrete efficiency metric for cost-aware deployment decisions.

2.title: Stop Making Models Bigger, Make Them Behave — Kobie Crawdord, Snorkel
2.author: AI Engineer
2.hook: Making a 4B parameter model outperform a 235B model on tool-use tasks through high-quality data + RL, not scale — demonstrates the data-quality-as-leverage pattern in production AI systems.

3.title: The Most AI-Pilled CEO We Know
3.author: Y Combinator
3.hook: Pedro's insight that "good AI products are agentic loops with tools" — and the shift from treating LLMs as precious/constrained (half a million lines of Rails for control) to "free the claw" (maximal context, token-generative agents) — maps directly to how Brex built their own AI product layer.

1.title: Claude Code Guide for Beginner by Claude Code Engineer Boris Cherny
1.author: BLD-Buluduo
1.hook: Claude Code works fully agentic at feature/function/file scope with zero setup (no indexing, code stays local), and Anthropic reduced technical onboarding from 2–3 weeks to 2–3 days by having hires do codebase Q&A first.

2.title: How AI Is Changing Code - Programmer Paul Ford | The Most Interesting Thing in AI
2.author: Nicholas Thompson and Atlantic Re:think
2.hook: Paul Ford contrasts how coding fundamentally changed in the last year (embraced AI tooling across the stack) vs. writing (mostly rejected it), and maps the shift from traditional spec→backend→frontend→QA workflows to AI-native iterative building where scope collapses and cost structure flips.
